{{Quote|You've met Thrawn. Any true warrior would have given up whatever was necessary for the chance to serve under him.|Voss Parck, to Mara Jade|<ref name="VotF" />}}
'''Voss Parck''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] that served as an [[Imperial officer/Legends|officer]] in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] and later [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], where he discovered the future [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] and later served as the [[Commander/Legends|commander]] in the [[Empire of the Hand]]. Hailing from a [[Navy/Legends|naval]] [[Parck family|family]] on [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]], Parck followed the expected career path and joined the Republic Navy, serving in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Shortly after the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Declaration of a New Order|became]] the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Parck came across Thrawn while chasing [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. Impressed by Thrawn's tactical abilities, Parck offered him a position in the Empire and took him back to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] was greatly pleased with Parck's find.

Parck remained attached to Thrawn's career in the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]], following the [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] on his deployment to subjugate the Unknown Regions and its myriad aggressors in the name of the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]]. Deeply devoted to and admiring of Thrawn, Parck served as his right-hand man throughout the mission, helping to bring many [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] under Imperial control and defeat the forces of [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Nuso Esva]]. When Thrawn [[Thrawn campaign|returned]] to known [[Realspace/Legends|space]] to take command of surviving forces under his [[Thrawn's confederation|confederation]], Parck was left behind as steward of the Empire of the Hand, a hidden power that Thrawn had carved out from [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].

Upon [[Battle of Bilbringi (9 ABY)|Thrawn's death]], Parck assumed sole command of the Empire of the Hand, continuing its mission to pacify the hostile civilizations in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]], which he regarded as essential to the future of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. When a [[Sinister Triumvirate|hoax]] proclaimed the [[Caamas Document Crisis|return]] of Thrawn [[19 ABY/Legends|ten years after]] his [[Death/Legends|death]], Parck cautiously opened relations with the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] at large, retaining high-level [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomatic]] ties even after the [[Flim (Human)|impostor]] was [[Battle of Yaga Minor (Galactic Civil War)|exposed]].

==Biography==
===Early career===
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]] to a wealthy and prominent Corulag [[Parck family|family]] with a long a proud lineage of [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] [[Captain/Legends|captaincy]]<ref name="AJ" /> and a tradition of [[Navy/Legends|naval]] service, Voss Parck entered the [[Corulag Academy]] to begin a career as a military [[Officer/Legends|officer]], following in the footsteps of his [[Voss Parck's father|father]] and [[Voss Parck's grandfather|grandfather]], who had both captained capital [[Starship/Legends|ships]].<ref name="Wizards.com" /> There, he trained alongside several siblings and cousins<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|13|Parck, Voss}}</ref> and carried on a rivalry with [[Voss Parck's cousin|one cousin in particular]], which would last into their military careers, though Parck generally came out behind.<ref name="ME" />

Within a few years of graduating the academy,<ref name="Wizards.com" /> Parck rose through the ranks and distuingished his service,<ref name="AJ" /> attaining the [[Military rank/Legends|rank]] of captain in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]], commanding the [[Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Strikefast/Legends|''Strikefast'']] by the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|end]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]<ref name="ME" /> in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. At the conclusion of the war, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] reorganized the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] with himself as its [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Parck, who was a great admirer of Palpatine, felt that the new [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] would bring positive change to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and continued his service in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]],<ref name="ME" /> leading the ''Strikefast'' on a long-range exploratory assignment.<ref name="Wizards.com" />

===The discovery of Thrawn===
{{Quote|You're still studying us, aren't you? Even now, as our prisoner, with little hope of escape, you're studying us.''"<br />"''Of course. You said it yourselves: you are potential dangers.''"<br />"''True. On the other hand, how better to neutralize a potential danger than from within it?|Voss Parck and Mitth'raw'nuruodo|<ref name="ME" />}}
[[File:Young_Thrawn.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Mitth'raw'nuruodo, as Parck found him]]
Around one [[Standard week/Legends|week]] after the [[Declaration of a New Order]], Parck and the ''Strikefast'' were in pursuit of the ''[[Starwayman]]'', a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Starship/Legends|ship]] suspected of carrying arms for an anti-Imperial resistance group. The smugglers made a blind [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jump into the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] in an effort to shake their pursuers, but Parck would not be deterred and gave pursuit.<ref name="ME" />

When the ships emerged from hyperspace, the crew of the ''Starwayman'' attempted to take refuge on a [[Unidentified planet (Thrawn's exile)/Legends|nearby planet]]. Parck ordered the launch of the ''Strikefast''{{'s}} [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] to pursue the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] into the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], but a problem with the launch racks prevented the launch of all but two of the [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], both of which were destroyed as they gave chase. The smugglers took refuge in a cave, and Parck dispatched a ground team and several starfighters to locate them and the two downed Imperial fighters. In the process, they discovered the abandoned dwelling of what appeared to be an unknown [[Species/Legends|species]]. Although he was exasperated by the additional [[Bureaucrat/Legends|bureaucracy]], Parck instructed his [[Commander/Legends|commander]] on the ground, [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Mosh Barris/Legends|Mosh Barris]], to handle the potential first contact situation in accordance with the Empire's [[Unknown Alien Encounters Orders]].<ref name="ME" />

Parck organized a technical team to send down in support of Barris. Meanwhile, Barris's [[Troop/Legends|troops]] found the body of one of the fighter [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]], clearly [[Death/Legends|killed]] and scavenged for technology. Shortly thereafter, mysterious explosions began to plague the Imperial ground camp, followed by the crash of another TIE. When Barris contacted him to report these new developments, Parck correctly deduced that the dead pilot's [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] had been stolen by the unknown [[Alien/Legends|aliens]], and had it cut out of the network.<ref name="ME" />

The next morning, Parck contacted Barris again. Barris had taken casualties and wished to simply raze the [[Tree/Legends|forest]] and pull out. Parck, however, was intent on finding the smugglers and the location of the resistance cell that they were supporting. Parck sent down two [[Squad/Legends|squads]] of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] to relieve Barris's [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]].<ref name="ME" />

[[File:Mist_Encounter.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Parck meets Thrawn for the first time.]]
At that point, the unidentified enemy&mdash;in fact an [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] by the name of [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] making clever use of Imperial supplies&mdash;began [[Jammer/Legends|jamming]] the ground forces. Cut off from communications with Parck and suffering casualties from the mysterious attacks, Barris ordered a retreat and returned to the ''Strikefast''. Parck quickly came to suspect that the alien Barris had encountered had stowed away aboard the [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] that had brought the surviving troops back from the surface. The captain took Barris to the [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] control bay, where he ordered that the lights be dimmed. Parck's suspicions were confirmed when Mitth'raw'nuruodo sneaked out of the shuttle.<ref name="ME" />

The Chiss was captured and questioned by Parck, who asked what he had hoped to accomplish by sneaking on board and also sought to find the methods by which Mitth'raw'nuruodo had outmaneuvered the Imperials, though he had to reign in the overly hostile and [[Humanocentrism|anti-alien]] Barris. Impressed by his resourcefulness and intrigued by the alien's desire to protect his people from assorted dangers, Parck offered him a position in the Imperial [[Fleet/Legends|Fleet]], phrasing it as an opportunity to put the Empire's resources to work against the threats of the Unknown Regions. Thrawn&mdash;as Mitth'raw'nuruodo decided to use his [[Core name/Legends|core name]] among the Imperials&mdash;accepted the offer, and Parck abandoned the [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]] for the smugglers in order to take what he saw as a more promising prize to the Emperor.<ref name="ME" />

===Thrawn and the Imperial Court===
{{Quote|You were one of the people every faction in the court used as an example of what not to do in the middle of a political fight. But then, those were the same people who also thought Palpatine sent Thrawn out here as a punishment. So what did they know?|Mara Jade, to Voss Parck|<ref name="VotF" />}}
Palpatine was in fact greatly pleased by Thrawn's recruitment; [[27 BBY/Legends|several years earlier]], Thrawn had aided Palpatine in destroying [[Outbound Flight Project|''Outbound Flight'']], a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] mission to explore beyond the known [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], as it had passed through the Unknown Regions, and Palpatine had twice tried unsuccessfully to recruit Thrawn since.<ref name="VotF" /> After bringing Thrawn to the Emperor, Parck's career saw a boost. On the other hand, Barris was shunted aside to backwater assignments, and his career plunged sharply, for which he always resented Parck.<ref name="MC">{{JournalCite|7|Missed Chance}}</ref>

Parck remained associated with Thrawn throughout the Chiss's swift rise through the Imperial ranks. When Thrawn, who was an active player in [[Imperial Court/Legends|Imperial Court]] [[Politics/Legends|politics]], was ready to return to the Unknown Regions and exert the Empire's influence, he and Palpatine staged a court scandal. The political fallout forced Thrawn into exile on a lowly mapping expedition to the Unknown Regions, or so it was thought. Parck, who backed Thrawn in a move so clearly unprofitable that it became notorious among the court, was likewise exiled with him<ref name="VotF" /> and demoted to the rank of commander.<ref name="CD" /> In fact, Parck was one of a few select individuals who knew that Thrawn's exile was staged<ref name="Wizards.com" /> and had quite deliberately put himself on the losing side in order to be assigned to the expedition, which was entirely orchestrated by Thrawn and Palpatine to allow Thrawn to conduct his mission of Imperial expansion in secrecy.<ref name="CD" />

===Mission to the Unknown Regions===
{{Quote|There are tremendous things out there waiting to be discovered, Captain. New species, rich worlds ripe for the taking, and any number of potential threats to the Empire. Our job is to find those threats, identify them&hellip; and eliminate them. [&hellip;] The Empire is on the move, Captain. And we're the ones who are taking it there.|Voss Parck, to Dagon Niriz|<ref name="CD" />}}
Parck was assigned to the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Admonitor]]'', Thrawn's new [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], as [[Executive officer/Legends|first officer]] to Captain [[Dagon Niriz]]. Niriz despised Parck for having brought the alien [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] to the Empire, deeming him arrogant. In the initial stages of the journey, Thrawn assigned Niriz to demeaning tasks and frequently countermanded Niriz's orders in such a way as to look passive and weak-willed. This was, in fact, part of a ploy, of which Parck was aware, to strain Niriz's patience and loyalty in a test.<ref name="CD" />

[[File:Ebruchi.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Creysis, who believed the ''Admonitor'' would be unable to save Parck from the Ebruchi victory feast.]]
Upon reaching the Unknown Regions, the ''Admonitor'' began scouting systems. In the fifteenth system searched the Imperials were approached by three unknown ships commanded by the [[Ebruchi]] [[Creysis]], who claimed to be the ruler of the system. Deducing that the Ebruchi were pirates, Thrawn devised a plan to deal with Creysis and find his superiors. Taking the opportunity to further test Niriz, Thrawn shared the details of his plan with Parck but not Niriz. The admiral convinced Creysis that the ''Admonitor'' was a colonization ship and dispatched Parck to negotiate with Creysis as part of a fictitious "[[Council of Colonists]]," taking a golden sculpture as a gift for Creysis's assistance. The admiral allowed Parck's [[Zeta-class long-range shuttle|''Zeta''-class shuttle]] to be captured by the Ebruchi. Niriz found Thrawn's performance intolerable, and so did [[General/Legends|General]] [[Larr Haverel]], the ship's [[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] commander. Haverel approached Niriz with a plan to mutiny, suggesting that their admiral could not possibly be so incompetent and must in fact be in league with Creysis. Niriz passed Thrawn's test when he refused to mutiny, sticking proudly to naval regulations and his sense of tradition and propriety.<ref name="CD" />

Parck took the opportunity to learn more about the Ebruchi while waiting for Thrawn to spring his trap, with Creysis telling the Imperial that he believed the ''Admonitor'' would be unable to save him from the upcoming [[Ebruchi victory feast]]. When Creysis sent the [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracker]]-equipped sculpture to his masters to demonstrate the ''Admonitor''{{'s}} worth as a target, Thrawn launched his TIE fighters against the pirates. At the same time, stormtroopers erupted from Parck's captured shuttle, easily overwhelming the assembled pirates and rescuing Parck and the shuttle's crew. Parck returned to the ''Admonitor'' as Thrawn [[Skirmish between the Admonitor and Creysis's scout squadron|demolished]] Creysis's forces. With Creysis defeated, Thrawn's forces proceeded to lay waste to the base of the pirate's superiors.<ref name="CD" />

After the battle was over, Niriz submitted his resignation as captain of the ''Admonitor''. Parck visited Niriz in his quarters, telling him that Thrawn had turned down his resignation. He informed the captain of the nature of Thrawn's test and the fact that Niriz had passed, as well as revealing the truth of their mission. Niriz took heart, and turned to the mission with much greater eagerness and respect for Thrawn.<ref name="CD" />

===Nuso Esva campaign===
{{Dialogue|Voss Parck|I sympathize with the Poln system, but I'm afraid I must refuse your request. We have orders of our own, and vital work to do.|Odo|This situation is more vital than anything you may be doing. A few hours' delay will surely not impact your mission.|Calo Drusan|If necessary, I can invoke Directive One-Oh-Three. In the absence of orders to the contrary, all fleet officers&mdash;|Voss Parck|I'm familiar with the directive. It doesn't apply to us.|Calo Drusan|You're part of the Imperial fleet, aren't you?|Voss Parck|Technically, we're detached from the fleet command structure. And as I said, Senior Captain Thrawn has his own set of orders that he needs to comply with.|attr=Parck responds to Odo's and Drusan's request for help in the Poln system|src=<ref name="CoO">''[[Choices of One]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Voss_Parck.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Voss Parck, early in his career]]
As they proceeded on their mission, more and more ships and resources were quietly transferred to Thrawn, giving him a small armada,<ref name="CD" /> and Parck was returned to his rank of captain.<ref name="CoO" /> By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> Thrawn's forces had come into conflict with [[Nuso Esva]],<ref name="CoO" /> a powerful [[Storm-hair]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] who had decimated several societies in the Unknown Regions.<ref name="CoF">{{StoryCite|story=Crisis of Faith|book=Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition}}</ref> Esva repeatedly turned down Thrawn's offer of a treaty and launched a campaign against some of the territories that Thrawn had pacified. The worlds under Esva's control stretched to the edge of the Empire, and Thrawn believed that Esva was planning to extend his influence into [[Imperial Space]]. Several [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the shock [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] victory at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Thrawn returned to the Empire to seek help in his campaign against Esva, leaving Parck in command of [[Task Force Admonitor|Task Force ''Admonitor'']] in his absence.<ref name="CoO" />

While Thrawn was away, Parck led an attack force comprised of the ''Admonitor'', two [[Strike-class medium cruiser|''Strike''-class medium cruisers]], and four [[Carrack-class light cruiser/Legends|''Carrack''-class light cruisers]] into [[Engagement at Teptixii|battle]] against elements of [[Nuso Esva's battle fleet]] at [[Teptixii]]. With the enemy fleet composed of eight [[Firekiln]] capital ships and twenty-seven escort vessels, Parck knew that they posed a serious threat to his forces. While he waited for reinforcements to arrive, Parck had his escorts sweep in front of the ''Admonitor'' to block fire from the Firekilns, while the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] focused on destroying the smaller enemy ships in order to leave the Firekilns vulnerable. Parck had the enemy ships pinned down when the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer [[Chimaera/Legends|''Chimaera'']] arrived in the [[Star system/Legends|system]]. Parck was surprised to find another Star Destroyer in the Unknown Regions, but with his reinforcements still twenty [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] away, he contacted Captain [[Calo Drusan]] aboard the ''Chimaera'' and requested help in finishing off Esva's fleet. Drusan agreed and, as the ''Chimaera'' moved to outflank the enemy, Esva's forces fled to hyperspace.<ref name="CoO" />

Following the [[Space warfare/Legends|battle]], Parck was contacted by Drusan and [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Odo, an apparent representative of the Emperor who was traveling aboard the ''Chimaera''. Odo relayed to Parck a request from General [[Kauf Ularno]] of [[Poln Major]] in the [[Candoras sector/Legends|Candoras sector]] for help in putting down a potential insurrection. Although not unsympathetic to the situation, Parck explained that his forces could not abandon their mission in the Unknown Regions and initially refused to help. However, upon receiving a transmission reporting the attempted [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] of the Candoras [[Sector/Legends|sector's]] [[Governor/Legends|governor]], [[Bidor Ferrouz]], by Rebel insurgents, Parck reluctantly agreed to assist. While the ''Admonitor'' traveled with the ''Chimaera'', Parck contacted the rest of Thrawn's fleet, instructing them to rendezvous in the [[Poln system/Legends|Poln system]]. He also sent a message to Thrawn to request his presence as Odo had requested it.<ref name="CoO" />

Unbeknownst to most of the Imperials, the situation on Poln Major had been orchestrated by Nuso Esva in an attempt to lure Thrawn's forces into a trap. Thrawn, however, was one step ahead of the warlord and was waiting in the Poln system aboard the [[DeepWater-class light freighter|''DeepWater''-class light freighter]] ''[[Lost Reef]]''. While Parck deployed his forces in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] of Poln Major, Esva made his move. Having infiltrated the ''Chimaera'' under the guise of Lord Odo, he killed Drusan and locked the ship on a collision course with the [[Golan I Space Defense Platform/Legends|Golan Space Defense SpaceGun]] defending the planet. Esva's fleet entered the system, and Parck moved to [[Battle of the Poln system|engage]] but, even after Thrawn and Commander [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]] of the ''Chimaera'' devised a plan to turn the Star Destroyer from its course and bring it back into the fight, the Imperials were heavily outgunned. Throughout the engagement, Thrawn and Esva mocked each other until Thrawn tricked Esva into revealing his intentions to dominate those who joined him. Only after relaying Esva's words to the Unknown Regions as a warning to others did Thrawn spring his own trap, sending a signal to the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], whose [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]] was waiting nearby. With the arrival of Vader's fleet, led by the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], the battle turned in the Imperials' favor. Esva's [[Eastern Fleet]] was decimated, though the warlord himself escaped and, with two more fleets operating in the Unknown Regions, remained a significant threat. After the battle, Thrawn rejoined Parck aboard the ''Admonitor'' and the pair returned to the Unknown Regions.<ref name="CoO" />

===The Empire of the Hand===
{{Dialogue|Voss Parck|The Chiss are his people, Mara&mdash;he has no interest in hurting them. Quite the opposite, in fact. He came back here to protect them.|Mara Jade|From what?|Kres'ten'tarthi|From what. You soft, complacent female. You think that because you lounge around your quiet worlds behind a ring of warships that the rest of the galaxy is a safe place to live? There are a hundred different threats out there that would freeze your blood if you knew about them. The ruling families can't stop them; neither can any other power in the region. If our people are to be protected, it's up to us.|attr=Voss Parck, Mara Jade and Kres'ten'tarthi|src=<ref name="VotF" />}}
[[File:Admonitor.jpg|thumb|right|220px|The ''Admonitor'', to which Parck was assigned]]
Under Thrawn, Parck participated in numerous campaigns against the various aggressors within the region<ref name="SQ">''[[Survivor's Quest]]''</ref> and was promoted to [[Captain of the Line/Legends|senior captain]]<ref name="CoF" /> at some point prior to [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]].<ref name="ERC" /> Eventually, Thrawn organized his conquests into the [[Empire of the Hand]].<ref name="SQ" /> Thrawn placed his headquarters on the planet [[Nirauan/Legends|Nirauan]], inside a building known as the [[Hand of Thrawn]] due to its distinctive shape.<ref name="VotF" /> It was this fortress that gave the Empire its name. It was made up not only of conquests, but also of planets that willingly joined. This empire, unlike Palpatine's, was tolerant of non-humans, fitting Thrawn's meritocratic style.<ref name="SQ" /> A major component of the Empire of the Hand was [[Syndic Mitth'raw'nuruodo's Household Phalanx]], an organization of Chiss supporters of Thrawn who worked on the margins of and even deep within Chiss society to recruit numerous warriors to Thrawn's cause.<ref name="VotF" />

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Emperor Palpatine was killed at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], and the Empire began to fragment and lose territory to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="NEC" /> Thrawn and Parck remained in the Unknown Regions to continue their work, but Thrawn, by this point a Grand Admiral, remained in contact with the mainstream Empire and had some degree of cooperation with [[Ysanne Isard]], Palpatine's eventual successor. It was this connection that gained the Empire of the Hand another crucial servant, Imperial fighter [[Ace/Legends|ace]] [[Baron of the Empire/Legends|Baron]] [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]].<ref name="VotF" />

Over the [[Standard year/Legends|years]], Thrawn stopped Nuso Esva's expansion and began to push the warlord back.<ref name="CoF" /> By 8 ABY,<ref name="ERC" /> the remnants of Esva's fleet were in hiding, and the warlord had taken refuge on the planet [[Quethold]], having manipulated the [[Quesoth]] [[Queen of the Red (8 ABY)|Queen of the Red]] into an alliance. Parck was charged with coordinating the search for Esva's scattered fleet, dispatching [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droids]] to investigate reports of possible activity. When a system was eliminated, probe droids would remain to ensure that Esva's forces could not flee there without the Empire of the Hand being alerted, reducing the number of potential hiding places. With Quethold under [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]], Thrawn consulted representatives of the [[Stromma]], allies of the Quesoth whose [[Oristrom|world]] had been liberated from Esva's rule by the Empire of the Hand, in preparation for a final battle against Esva.<ref name="CoF" />

Parck joined Thrawn's senior officers and representatives of the [[Stromma council]] at a strategy session aboard the ''Admonitor'', With the Queen of the Red due to be replaced as Quesoth ruler by the [[Queen of the White]] in two years, [[Stromma Council Liaison]] [[Nyama]] favored maintaining the blockade, but, with several other threats requiring the Empire of the Hand's attention, Thrawn could not afford a lengthy siege, and sought a decisive victory. The Stromma used their contacts within Quesoth dissidents to acquire [[Holocamera/Legends|holocam]] footage of Nuso Esva's chambers in [[Red City]]'s [[Dwelling of Guests]], which they presented to Thrawn and Parck in a subsequent meeting aboard the ''Admonitor''. Thrawn anticipated that Esva would attempt to set a trap for his forces at the western edge of the [[City/Legends|city]], and planned to send his [[Tank/Legends|tanks]] into the trap, while sending stormtroopers into the city from another direction to attack Esva's forces from behind when they engaged the tanks. Despite Parck's best efforts to convince him, Nyama refused to commit Stromma forces to the attack, but Thrawn decided to press ahead without them.<ref name="CoF" />

Parck's search for Esva's remaining ships prevented him from being involved in the planning for the [[Attack on the Red City|assault]] on Red City, but he joined Thrawn to observe the battle aboard the ''Admonitor'' the day after the meeting with the Stromma. During the battle, Thrawn used fake orders broadcast in [[Quesoth Soldier Speak]] to trick Esva into thinking that the [[Queen of the Red|Queen]] had betrayed him; Esva killed the [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] and was subsequently killed by her [[Quesoth Soldier|Soldiers]]. Although Esva was defeated, Parck was concerned about possible reprisals from his followers, the [[Chosen (Nuso Esva)|Chosen]] warriors. Thrawn, however, doubted that they would present much of a threat with their leader gone and decided that the [[Time/Legends|time]] had come for him to return to the Empire and take [[Thrawn campaign|command]] of the [[Thrawn's confederation|Imperial Fleet]]. While Thrawn left to rendezvous with Captain Gilad Pellaeon on the ''Chimaera'', Parck took the ''Admonitor'' to the [[Chaos Triangle]] to cleanup what the Grand Admiral referred to as Esva's "legacy."<ref name="CoF" />

In Thrawn's absence, Parck became an admiral and took command of the Empire of the Hand. Thrawn remained in contact with Parck, who was fully appraised of Thrawn's strategies as [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|supreme commander]]. Conversely, Thrawn, who was well-known for his centralization of information within himself and minimal dispersal of it to his subordinates, informed no one within the Empire of the existence of the Empire of the Hand. This meant that when Thrawn was [[Battle of Bilbringi (9 ABY)|unexpectedly killed]]<ref name="VotF" /> in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]] by his [[Rukh/Legends|bodyguard]],<ref name="NEC" /> the Empire of the Hand's existence was completely lost to the galaxy at large. Before Thrawn's death, the Grand Admiral left instructions that, were he ever to be reported dead, Parck was to continue his mission in the Unknown Regions and wait ten years for his return. As a result, Parck kept his attention turned outward as he continued the fight in the Unknown Regions, choosing not to reveal himself and the Empire of the Hand's plentiful resources to the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]]. Not even the [[Operation Shadow Hand|return of Palpatine]] drew Parck from the Unknown Regions.<ref name="VotF" />

While waiting for Thrawn's return, Parck continued the Empire of the Hand's relentless campaigns against anything which threatened the Empire or the [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Ascendancy]], whether the Chiss desired their help or not. Parck's top assistants in this period were General Fel and the Chiss officer [[Kres'ten'tarthi]], the commander of the Household Phalanx.<ref name="VotF" /> Parck also had some contact with the Chiss Ascendancy, despite the fact that the existence of the Empire of the Hand was officially unrecognized. [[Chaf family/Legends|Chaf family]] [[Aristocra/Legends|Aristocra]] [[Chaf'orm'bintrano]] "Formbi" was at least one highly-placed Chiss official who was on speaking terms with Parck.<ref name="SQ" />

===The return of Thrawn===
{{Quote|Many years ago Thrawn told us that if he was ever reported dead we should keep at our labors here and in the Unknown Regions, and to look for his return ten years afterward.|Voss Parck, to Mara Jade|<ref name="VotF" />}}
[[File:CloneThrawn.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade infiltrate the Hand of Thrawn.]]
[[19 ABY/Legends|Ten years after]] his death, as promised, Parck's known space contacts brought to his ears rumors of the return of Thrawn. Parck immediately dispatched [[Scout/Legends|scout]] ships to search out former [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]], whom he saw as a perfect intermediary due to her Imperial past, New Republic connections, and close relationship with the galaxy's largest [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]], [[Talon Karrde]]. Having had no contact with Thrawn, Parck was unsure of the accuracy of the rumors and wished to be completely certain that the Grand Admiral had returned before revealing the Empire of the Hand's existence to the Imperial Remnant. Parck was in fact right to doubt, as the "[[Flim (Human)|Thrawn]]" of the rumors was in fact an [[Con artist/Legends|impostor]], hired as part of a [[Sinister Triumvirate|scheme]] by [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Vilim Disra]] to [[Caamas Document Crisis|seize power]] within the Remnant. The timing was coincidental; Thrawn's actual promise was to be fulfilled by a [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo (clone)|clone]] grown in a secret sublevel of the Hand of Thrawn, to be awakened by a timed system which was continually reset by Thrawn up to his death.<ref name="VotF" />

By triangulating the vectors of two of the scout ships, Jade followed them back to Nirauan, but was shot down over the planet. [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] was contacted by Karrde and set off to rescue her. Eventually the two of them [[Mission to Nirauan|infiltrated]] the Hand of Thrawn, where Jade was captured and brought before Parck, Fel and Kres'ten'tarthi. Parck, by now an old and [[Color/Legends|gray]]-haired man, revealed the basic history of the Empire of the Hand to Jade and offered her a position within it, stressing the vital nature of its mission. Jade, however, refused the offer. With further reports that Thrawn had returned to the Imperial [[Capital/Legends|capital]] world of [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]], Parck decided to risk contact with the Empire. To stop Jade interfering, Parck ordered her detained until they had contacted Bastion and Fel suggested wounding Jade to force her into a Jedi [[Force healing/Legends|healing trance]] which would prevent her escape. Before Parck's Chiss guards could act, however, the conference was broken up by Skywalker, who cut his way into the room and rescued Jade, escaping to the hidden sublevels of the base. The [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of Thrawn was killed in a flood of the lower levels caused by Skywalker and Jade's escape attempt, and before Parck could dispatch a scout craft to Bastion, Jade remotely steered her [[Jade's Fire|ship]] into the Hand's hangar, disabling the base's ships. Parck was left to clean up his damaged base, while the false Thrawn was exposed before Parck could make contact, keeping knowledge of the Empire of the Hand and its vast territories limited to Skywalker and Jade.<ref name="VotF" />

In the chaos and vulnerability immediately after the attack on the Hand's hangars, the Hand was assaulted by a well-organized gang of pirates and fell to them, forcing Parck to evacuate the planet.<ref name="RSBF">{{GamerCite|7|Red Sky, Blue Flame}}</ref> However, this did not last, as Parck was back on Nirauan<ref name="SQ" /> by [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]].<ref name="ERC" />

===Diplomatic dealings===
{{Quote|What makes you think Parck even wants diplomatic relations with the Chiss?''"<br />"''We do. Very much.|Mara Jade Skywalker and Chak Fel|<ref name="SQ" />}}
Knowledge of the Empire of the Hand slowly leaked out, with Skywalker and Jade informing New Republic [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]]. The Imperial Remnant, under Thrawn's former protégé Gilad Pellaeon, also had some contact with Parck, though he chose not to ally himself with any particular group or engage in serious diplomatic relations. One group with which he did wish to have better relations was the Chiss Ascendancy, whose citizens provided much of the Empire of the Hand's manpower and which the Empire of the Hand existed to protect. However, as Thrawn was an exile from the Ascendancy and Chiss military doctrine refused to recognize the Empire of the Hand's tactics as moral, relations remained strained and unofficial despite Parck's wish for better cooperation.<ref name="SQ" />

[[File:Chiss_Ascendancy.svg|thumb|right|300px|Parck desired to have better relations with the Chiss Ascendancy. (logo pictured)]]
In 22 ABY,<ref name="ERC" /> Parck was notified by the Chiss that the remains of ''Outbound Flight'' had been found. The Chiss intended to make a conciliatory diplomatic event out of the mission to recover its wreckage, and Parck forwarded their message to Skywalker and Jade&mdash;now [[Wedding of Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade|married]] to Skywalker&mdash;who were invited along as representatives of the [[New Jedi Order|Jedi]] and New Republic. However, his message was intercepted by one of Talon Karrde's [[Dean Jinzler|employees]] who had had [[Jinzler family|family]] aboard ''Outbound Flight''. Consequently, the Skywalkers arrived over Nirauan instead of at the rendezvous point contained in the message. They spoke with Parck, who had overcome whatever resentment the destruction of his hangar might have caused him, and Parck informed them of the Chiss Ascendancy's request. Unbenknownst to the Skywalkers, Formbi was using the diplomatic mission to lure the [[Vagaari/Legends|Vagaari]]&mdash;a species of nomadic [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]] operating in the region&mdash;into an attack, allowing the Chiss to declare war on the threat, since Chiss military doctrine did not accept the idea of the preemptive strike. Knowing that the mission would come under attack, Parck sent his own representatives to the meeting: Commander [[Chak Fel]] and the four stormtroopers of the [[501st Legion (Empire of the Hand)|501st Legion's]] [[Unit Aurek-Seven]]. Fel and his [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] were allegedly there to protect the Skywalkers, but were secretly charged with supporting Chaf own forces.<ref name="SQ" />

By the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], General [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] Soontir Fel had become the public face of the Empire of the Hand in its dealings with the New Republic, and Parck had largely disappeared from the scene.<ref name="DT2">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide II: Ruin]]''</ref> By around the end of the war, the Empire of the Hand had disappeared from the galactic scene, leaving Nirauan abandoned. Speculation at the time included the Empire of the Hand's destruction or absorption by the Chiss Ascendancy. Formbi suggested to Luke Skywalker that the Empire of the Hand had served its purpose and would rise again when needed.<ref name="TJK">''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]''</ref> Soontir Fel joined the Chiss Ascendancy proper and Luke Skywalker expressed a belief to [[Chief Navigator]] [[Peita Aabe]] of the Chiss Ascendancy that Parck had also "joined the Chiss."<ref name="FH2">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic II: Refugee]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|The task ahead of us is far too serious for anyone to waste time on anything as petty as politics or personal gain.|Voss Parck, to Mara Jade|<ref name="VotF" />}}
[[File:Thrawn-DB.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Grand Admiral Mitth'raw'nuruodo, Parck's patron and role model]]
An avowed Palpatinist at the dawn of the Empire, Voss Parck believed strongly in order and obedience to government. He was committed to the Imperial Fleet as an institution and resented what he regarded as meddlesome political oversight which handcuffed its effectiveness.<ref name="ME" /> Showing great promise during his time at the Academy,<ref name="Wizards.com" /> Parck began his career as a dutiful and ambitious [[Imperial officer/Legends|officer]], seeking promotion in the Fleet.<ref name="ME" /> Despite achieving the rank of captain with a few years, however, Parck's career was entirely ordinary until his chance encounter with Thrawn<ref name="Wizards.com" /> and his priorities subsequently changed.<ref name="CD" />

Parck willingly accepted demotion<ref name="CD" /> and disgrace among the Imperial Court to join Thrawn in his mission to the Unknown Regions, where he became a zealous crusader determined to combat the region's myriad enemies, with no concern for personal gain or advancement. He genuinely believed in the cause, enough to unsettle Mara Jade during their interview.<ref name="VotF" /> He was convinced that the mission of the Empire of the Hand was truly vital to securing the Empire and the galaxy as a whole,<ref name="CD" /> to the point that he was reluctant to abandon it to assist the Empire in preventing an insurrection in the Candoras sector.<ref name="CoO" /> Such was Parck's level of devotion to Thrawn that, after the Grand Admiral's death, Parck waited patiently for his promised return rather than reveal the Empire of the Hand's existence to the Imperial Remnant.<ref name="VotF" />

Though Parck began as Thrawn's discoverer, he quickly found the relationship reversed. Thrawn was already known to Emperor Palpatine and was greatly sought by him. Thrawn was promoted swiftly while Parck was left in his wake. Thrawn remained quite loyal to Parck, however, keeping him as his right-hand man throughout his career. Parck returned this loyalty in turn. He was deeply impressed by Thrawn's abilities and willingly shared in his supposed exile to the Unknown Regions,<ref name="VotF" /> keeping faith in his commander's abilities, even when he did not fully understand his plans.<ref name="CoF" /> Even after Thrawn's death, Parck continued to be loyal to him and remained utterly assured of his promise to return, to the point that Mara Jade considered him almost delusional.<ref name="VotF" />

Parck was a highly intelligent man with a well-developed deductive skill similar to, though not as extensive as, that of Thrawn. Parck had in fact out-thought Thrawn at least partially in their first meeting, correctly predicting his stowing away on the shuttle.<ref name="ME" /><ref name="VotF" /> Thrawn, who was generally miserly with information, kept Parck within his confidences throughout his career and trusted him implicitly, often revealing details of his plans to Parck which were not known to his other protégés, Dagon Niriz and Gilad Pellaeon,<ref name="CD" /><ref name="VotF" /> and valued Parck's keen mind, along with his steadfast loyalty.<ref name="Wizards.com" />

Besides a firm grasp of tactics, strategy, negotiation, and information-gathering, Parck spoke multiple [[Language/Legends|languages]] in addition to his native [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], including [[Cheunh/Legends|Cheunh]], [[Honoghran]], [[Twi'leki/Legends|Twi'leki]], and [[Zabraki/Legends|Zabraki]].<ref name="Wizards.com" /> He could also understand [[Quesoth Common Speak]].<ref name="CoF" />

==Equipment==
During the early days of the Galactic Empire, Parck served as captain of the ''Victory''-class Star Destroyer ''Strikefast''.<ref name="ME" /> Following his demotion to commander, he served under Captain Dagon Niriz aboard the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer ''Admonitor''.<ref name="CD" /> Throughout his career, Parck wore a standard [[Imperial officer's uniform/Legends|Imperial officer's uniform]],<ref name="Wizards.com" /> complete with [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|rank insignia]] and [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinder]].<ref name="ERC" /> By his time in command of the Empire of the Hand, Parck carried a Chiss comlink and was armed with a Chiss [[Charric/Legends|charric]] and [[Knife/Legends|knife]].<ref name="Wizards.com" />

==Behind the scenes==
The character of Voss Parck was created by [[Timothy Zahn]] for the short story "[[Mist Encounter]]," published in [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 7|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 7]] in [[August]] [[1995]].<ref name="ME" /> Parck's position in relation to that of Dagon Niriz is unclear. At the outset of their expedition to the Unknown Regions, Niriz outranked Parck. However, Parck was clearly acting as Thrawn's right-hand man during ''[[Command Decision]]'', while Niriz was left out of the loop.<ref name="CD" /> ''[[Choices of One]]'' shows Parck once more holding the rank of captain and in command of the ''Admonitor'', while the Zahn short story "[[Side Trip]]," set after the events of ''Choices of One'', shows Niriz as captain of the ''Admonitor'' when Thrawn returns to known space in order to execute a small mission on behalf of Lord Vader.<ref name="CoO" /><ref name="ST">"[[Side Trip]]"</ref> Parck is once again acting as captain of the ''Admonitor'' in Zahn's ''[[Crisis of Faith]]'', a [[2011]] novella published in the [[Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition|20th Anniversary Edition]] of his [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'', the ship's latest chronological appearance.<ref name="CoF" />
